notes:
Account summary: enterprise fintech platform (digital banking + conversational assistant). Very cost-sensitive on token units but uptime/latency are critical for customer-facing chat. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated primarily for predictable throughput and isolation.

Key negotiation themes: throughput guarantees (min tokens/sec), concurrency caps per model, burst policy parameters, and reserved GPU planning. They want deterministic billing for reserved capacity and clear breakpoints for falling back to hosted or cheaper variants.

CRM-style notes / call snippets:
- 2024-11-14 intro (Sofia): overview of architecture and compliance needs. Interested in 3-tier routing (primary dedicated, regional fallback, hosted burst).
- "We cannot tolerate p95 latency > 300ms during peak auth flows" — VP Eng (call 11/18).
- 2024-11-18 technical deep-dive (Diego): network topology, KMS requirements (customer keys), and encryption at rest details. Sent security questionnaire (drive link).
- 2024-11-29 SLA workshop: went line-by-line on throughput calc. Praesidium insists on a contractual minimum tokens/sec across reserved pool. Discussed concurrency shaping.
- 2024-12-02 POC kickoff (internal infra): agreed to 2-week smoke with synthetic traffic, then 2-week pilot with production traces.
- 2024-12-04 pricing review: initial reserved GPU ask (8x A100 equiv) vs Redwood sizing recommendation (start 12x for headroom).

Quotes / negotiation points:
- "We need a firm min tokens/sec for billing and operational alerts — can't have token dips under 40k without mitigation" (SRE lead).
- Redwood proposal: baseline 60k tokens/sec sustained across the dedicated pool, with burst allowance up to 120k tokens/sec for 10 minutes subject to quota/credit usage.
- Praesidium counter: allow burst but require clear throttling semantics, per-tenant concurrency caps, and guaranteed fallback latency when bursting to hosted.

Materials shared: pricing deck (drive:/Praesidium/Redwood_Dedicated_RFP_v1.pdf), SLA diff matrix (drive:/Praesidium/SLA-diff-matrix.xlsx), security FAQ link stub.

POC acceptance criteria (high level):
- sustained aggregate throughput >= 55k tokens/sec for 48hr window under typical mix (chat 60%, rerank 30%, embeddings 10%)
- p95 latency <= 300ms for chat requests <= 1024 tokens under target concurrency
- successful KMS integration and audit log ingestion to their SIEM
- documented burst behaviour and no silent throttles observed during 2x sustained bursts

Sales / next steps: redline throughput SLA draft, Redwood to provide quantized sizing (GPU types + count), schedule network e2e test (2h) with Praesidium infra team, legal to exchange initial terms by 2024-12-12.

throughput_requirements: Min aggregated tokens/sec (contractual): 60,000 sustained across dedicated pool
Per-tenant concurrency cap: 60-80 concurrent inference streams per service (configurable)
Burst policy: up to 2x sustained throughput (i.e., 120k tokens/sec) for 10 continuous minutes, subject to credits and notification
Reservable GPU footprint: initial proposal 12 x A100(80GB) equiv; customer requested 8 x A100 to start with scaling floor
Latency SLOs: p50 < 90ms; p95 < 300ms for chat workloads <= 1024 tokens; p95 < 500ms for long-form (>1024 tokens)
Failover semantics: when capacity exceeded, automatic routing to regional hosted pool with documented added latency; customer requires no silent failures
poc_plan: Week 0: baseline sizing + network prep; exchange test certs and KMS setup
Week 1-2: synthetic load tests to validate sustained throughput and burst handling
Week 3-4: production-trace pilot with sampled traffic; measure p95/p50 and concurrency behavior
Acceptance: 48hr sustained run meeting throughput and latency thresholds; security checklist signed off
